Quick triage notes (preliminary):

- Root symptom: repeated first-token stalls (~2.5s) observed when new GPU-backed serving instances are created to handle burst. These show up as long delays in model handshake / CUDA context init and initial KV cache population. Subsequent tokens are normal.
- Likely trigger: autoscaler created fresh instances during customer burst; our current warmup policy relies on library-level lazy CUDA init which can add 1.5–3s on some GPU types under heavy noisy-neighbor memory pressure.
- Contributing factor: warm pool size for hosted-api us-west1 was at a conservative setting after recent capacity optimization; when burst > warm pool, we spin new instances causing the handshake penalty.
- Evidence: attached warmup logs and a set of traces (extracts below).

Suggested mitigations (short term):
1) Route FinLedger traffic to a pre-warmed fallback model variant (quantized, lower-memory) while we deploy a warm pool bump. This reduces p95 for customer immediately.
2) Increase warm pool min in us-west1 from 4 -> 12 for 72h while we observe.
3) Flip a library-level CUDA eager-init flag in the serving runtime as an experiment to remove per-instance handshake cost (requires rollout to hosted pools).

I'll prioritize a targeted warm-pool bump and a routing change for this customer's cids.

Dev Patel
SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Samir — thank you again for flagging this and for the trace bundle. We take this seriously — apologies for the customer impact. Quick update and plan:

Summary:
- What happened: During your payroll surge on 2026-12-15, our Hosted API autoscaler created additional GPU-backed instances. A small proportion of those instances experienced an elevated per-instance handshake/CUDA-init latency (~2–3s) on first-request, which increased p95/p99 for some of your requests.
- Immediate impact: transient timeouts (502/504) and elevated tail latency for first requests in the affected window.

Actions taken (immediate):
1) We routed FinLedger traffic to a pre-warmed fallback model variant in us-west1 to reduce first-request stalls (already applied).
2) We increased the warm pool minimum in us-west1 from 4 -> 12 for 72 hours to cover expected burst patterns (rolled 2026-12-16 09:30 UTC).
3) SRE is running a targeted experiment to enable eager CUDA-init on a subset of hosted pools to validate handshake reduction; results expected within 48–72h.

Next steps (per your procurement request):
- We will deliver a one-page executive summary and an SLA incident acknowledgement to contracts@finledger.com by EOD Monday.
- Post-incident remediation: Eng will propose a permanent fix (runtime eager-init + smarter warm-pool autoscaling by traffic fingerprint) with a timeline and roll plan in the post-mortem.
- Commercial: we propose a provisional credit to address the impacted window — Dev/Sales to finalize amount; legal/procurement included.

Attachments: warmup-logs-20261216.txt, finledger-traces-20261215-09.zip, SLA-exemption-request.docx

I'll follow up Monday with the exec one-pager and the formal acknowledgement. Please let me know if you'd prefer a call tomorrow to walk through the mitigation.
